# CLI reference: `bhms`

Every command of the `bhms` command line, its arguments and options, as the installed program defines them. `python -m bhms` is the same program without the console script.

Targets (first argument of ls/describe/read/call/ops/wait/cancel/resolve/stop, or --url / BHMS_URL): unix:/path, ws://host:port, http://host:port/bhms, a server .py or a gateway .toml. Exit status: 0 ok, 1 refused or failed, 2 usage, 3 not settled (running or unknown).

The one-shot commands (`call`, `cancel`, `describe`, `ls`, `ops`, `read`, `resolve`, `stop`, `wait`) accept the target as their first argument (`bhms call server.py stage-z move_to target=5`) or through `--url`/`BHMS_URL`.

| Command | Summary |
|---|---|
| [`bhms ls`](#bhms-ls) | List devices. |
| [`bhms describe`](#bhms-describe) | Describe one device: actions with units and bounds, properties, effects, leases, stop behaviour. |
| [`bhms read`](#bhms-read) | Read a property: value, unit, evidence, quality and age. |
| [`bhms call`](#bhms-call) | Invoke an action: `bhms call pump-1 dispense volume=50 --key run-42`. |
| [`bhms ops`](#bhms-ops) | List recent operations. |
| [`bhms wait`](#bhms-wait) | Wait for an operation to settle (exit 3 when it has not by the timeout). |
| [`bhms cancel`](#bhms-cancel) | Ask an operation to stop (a request: check the reported cancel state). |
| [`bhms resolve`](#bhms-resolve) | For operators: ask the device again about an unknown operation, or resolve it with evidence. |
| [`bhms stop`](#bhms-stop) | Stop devices now (their stop procedure, their operations, their leases). Not an emergency stop. |
| [`bhms doctor`](#bhms-doctor) | Check the environment and, with a target, connectivity, identity and device descriptions. |
| [`bhms new`](#bhms-new) | Scaffold a device server and its test: `bhms new demo && bhms dev demo/server.py`. |
| [`bhms dev`](#bhms-dev) | Start the interactive inspector: devices, describe, read, invoke with prompts, live operations and events. |
| [`bhms gateway`](#bhms-gateway) | Run a gateway: aggregates device servers behind one endpoint with policy, leases and a journal. |
| [`bhms mcp`](#bhms-mcp) | Serve the eight BHMS agent tools to any MCP client (Claude, Cursor, ...): `bhms mcp demo/server.py`. |
| [`bhms conformance`](#bhms-conformance) | Run the BHMS conformance suite against a server, gateway or agent bridge. |
| [`bhms bench`](#bhms-bench) | Measure round-trip latency of a target. |

## bhms ls

| `--text` | `TEXT` |  |  | Words in name, summary or tags. |

| `--tag` | `TEXT` |  |  |  |

## bhms resolve

```text no-run
bhms resolve [OPTIONS] OPERATION
```

For operators: ask the device again about an unknown operation, or resolve it with evidence.

Without --state the server only re-runs reconciliation. With --state and --basis it records your resolution when
the device still cannot say (device evidence always wins). Needs the admin or operations:resolve scope.
Exit status: 0 resolved, 3 still unknown, 1 refused, 2 usage.

| Argument | Required | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `OPERATION` | yes | The unknown operation. |

| Option | Value | Default | Environment | Help |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--url`, `-u` | `TEXT` |  | `BHMS_URL` | Server URL, server .py or gateway .toml. |
| `--token` | `TEXT` |  | `BHMS_TOKEN` | Bearer token (prefer the environment). |
| `--state` | `TEXT` |  |  | completed or failed: record this resolution if the device cannot say what happened. Needs --basis. |
| `--basis` | `TEXT` |  |  | What was inspected, by whom, and what was found. |
| `--effect` | `TEXT` |  |  | unverified (an operator's report never verifies; use --nothing-happened for effect none). |
| `--result` | `TEXT` |  |  | With --state completed: the result as JSON, valid for the action's output. |
| `--nothing-happened` | flag |  |  | With --state failed: there is proof that the device did not act (effect none). |
| `--json` | flag |  |  | Machine-readable output: {summary, data \| error}. |

## bhms gateway

```text no-run
bhms gateway [OPTIONS] CONFIG [CONFIG]
```

Run a gateway: aggregates device servers behind one endpoint with policy, leases and a journal.

`bhms gateway check-policy <config>` does not serve: it starts the configured upstreams, reads their devices and
lists, per principal and scope, which devices and actions each scope matches, with a warning for every scope that
matches nothing (for example `invoke:bench/*`, which must be `invoke:bench/*/*` behind a gateway) and for a
principal that may act on a device it may not stop.

| Argument | Required | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIG` | yes | Gateway TOML (see examples/bhms/gateway.toml), or the word check-policy followed by the TOML. |
| `[CONFIG]` | no | With check-policy: the gateway TOML whose policy is checked. |

| Option | Value | Default | Environment | Help |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--verbose`, `-v` | flag |  |  | Log at INFO. |
| `--json` | flag |  |  | check-policy: print the report as JSON. |
| `--strict` | flag |  |  | check-policy: exit 1 when there is a warning. |

## bhms conformance

```text no-run
bhms conformance [OPTIONS] [TARGET]
```

Run the BHMS conformance suite against a server, gateway or agent bridge.

| Argument | Required | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `TARGET` | no | Target to test (see --help epilog). |

| Option | Value | Default | Environment | Help |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--profile`, `-p` | `TEXT` (repeatable) |  |  | One of core, authority, leases, events, programs, registry, gateway, compact, ws, http, agent; repeatable. |
| `--json` | `PATH` |  |  | Write the JSON report here ('-' for stdout). |
| `--strict` | flag |  |  | Validate every message against the JSON Schema. |
| `--allow-effects` | flag |  |  | Let generic checks execute actions on devices that are not the conformance device. |
| `--token` | `TEXT` |  | `BHMS_TOKEN` | Bearer token (prefer the environment). |
| `--seed` | `INTEGER` |  |  | Seed for generated keys (reported for reproduction). |
| `--only` | `TEXT` (repeatable) |  |  | Run only checks whose name contains this; repeatable. |
| `--device` | `TEXT` |  |  | Agent profile: a BHMS target serving the same devices the bridge fronts (fault injection, counters). |
| `--keep-state` | `TEXT` |  |  | Directory for the state of fixtures the runner starts. |
| `--physical` | flag |  |  | State in the report that the devices are physical. |
| `--commit` | `TEXT` | `unknown` |  | Implementation commit to record in the report. |
| `--allow-unproven` | flag |  |  | Exit 0 although MUST rows that a check could have proven were skipped (the report still says the claim is unsupported). |
| `--conformance-device` | `TEXT` (repeatable) |  |  | Device id asserted to be a conformance device (behind a gateway the extension is not visible); repeatable. |
| `--upstream` | `TEXT` (repeatable) |  |  | NAMESPACE=TARGET: a direct connection to the conformance device behind a gateway namespace (fault injection); repeatable. |
| `--function-tools` | `PATH` |  |  | Agent profile: JSON list of the OpenAI function-tool definitions of the bridge's adapter (BHMS-AGT-050). |
| `--physical-ok` | flag |  |  | With --physical: allow checks that move or change the devices. |
| `--device-command` | `TEXT` |  |  | With a conformance-device fixture: launch this command (split like a shell line) instead of this SDK's own device, e.g. "node dist/src/testing/conformanceDevice.js". It must accept [URL] [--state-dir DIR] [--memory] [--principals FILE]. |
| `--verbose`, `-v` | flag |  |  | Also list passed checks' requirements and skipped rows. |
| `--coverage` | flag |  |  | Print the requirement coverage table and exit. |
